items.title: Live: Iran denies Trump's claims of 'very good' talks as initial strike deadline passes
items.description: US President Donald Trump says there have been "major points of agreement" in US-Iran talks to end the war, but Iran denies those claims. Follow live.

items.title: Two ships scrapped for parts have suddenly reappeared in the Strait of Hormuz
items.description: Iran has effectively blocked the only way out of the Persian Gulf, leaving about 3,000 ships stranded. But two zombie ships appear to have sailed in and out of the Gulf through the Strait of Hormuz.

items.title: Lebanon's justice minister says Hezbollah serves as 'pretext' for Israeli attacks
items.description: Lebanon's justice minister accuses the Iranian-backed militant group Hezbollah of effectively giving Israel an excuse to attack the country amid threats of an Israeli occupation of the south.

items.title: It's TACO Tuesday as Trump presses pause. Here's what you should know
items.description: The ABC's Middle East correspondent Matthew Doran is in Beirut and is providing daily updates on the Middle East war.

items.title: Alice Springs locals conflicted over spy base's role in Iran war
items.description: Residents with family in the Middle East are grappling with the part the highly secretive Pine Gap base may be playing in the Iran war from their own backyard.

items.title: Live: Albanese, EU boss give green light to free trade deal
items.description: After almost a decade of negotiations, Prime Minister Anthony Albanese has confirmed Australia has struck a free trade agreement with the European Union. Follow live.

items.title: Denmark's PM stared down Donald Trump. Voters look set to reward her
items.description: When Donald Trump threatened to annex Greenland, Denmark leader Mette Frederiksen was flailing in the polls. Having stood up to the US president, she looks to have salvaged her political career.

items.title: Clinicians told to not override aged care algorithm
items.description: A new algorithm for deciding how much aged care support people can receive to stay living at home is being blamed for reducing care to older Australians.

items.title: EV drivers smug as the world learns painful lesson on fossil fuel dependence
items.description: From UN leaders to former Australian Defence Force chiefs, a growing chorus of voices argues that dependence on fossil fuels is not just a climate issue, but a national security risk — exposing countries to volatile prices and supply shocks.

items.title: Live: Global stocks lift after Trump about face, ASX rises
items.description: Australian shares are higher, with the ASX 200 up sharply at the start of today's session before easing after global stock indices lifted when Donald Trump postponed strikes on Iranian infrastructure. Follow live.

items.title: Will Trump obliterate financial markets?
items.description: Donald Trump appears to be fast running out of exits on his Iran war folly.

items.title: When the 'orange people' moved in, this tiny WA town fought back
items.description: When the Rajneesh sect moved into a small town in Western Australia, the group didn't count on the strength of the local community fighting back.

items.title: Teachers in Victoria go on strike for the first time in 13 years
items.description: Hundreds of state schools could close or face significant disruptions today, as teachers walk off the job for the first time over a decade, says the Australian Education Union.

items.title: BOM says more rain causing 'significant river level rises' in soaked NT
items.description: BOM is warning major riverine flooding could follow the "moderate to heavy rainfall" dumped across the NT by ex-Tropical Cyclone Narelle.

items.title: They had doubts, but this couple has grown a native forest from scratch
items.description: Some become grey nomads, others learn a language or some other skill. After retirement, this couple took on creating a native forest. But, as John and Annette were to find out, there is "no textbook".

items.title: Would you pass Year 9 maths? Try our NAPLAN-inspired quiz
items.description: Australian students have just been put to the test with NAPLAN. Now it's your turn to see how you'd go in their shoes.

items.title: Why we decided to buy a share of our in-laws' house
items.description: Experts say housing affordability is pushing people to rethink the rule book on property ownership.

items.title: 'Prioritised institution over students': Top university savaged
items.description: University of Technology Sydney is warned over "reprisal" action against a student who highlighted the university's failure to act on reviews into its gender-based violence policies.

items.title: Iranian terror group claims responsibility for attack on Jewish ambulances in London
items.description: An Iranian-aligned terror group is claiming responsibility for an arson attack on Jewish ambulances in London, according to an intelligence website.

items.title: TACO Trump strikes again with sudden Iran backdown
items.description: After threatening to "obliterate" Iran's power plants, Donald Trump's sudden backdown is again fuelling TACO taunts.

items.title: Controller appears to say 'I messed up' after deadly runway crash
items.description: Audio recordings from New York's LaGuardia airport reveal an air traffic controller appearing to admit he "messed up" just moments after an Air Canada Express regional jet crashed into a fire truck, killing the pilot and co-pilot.

items.title: Broad public support to stop 'undue influence' in politics
items.description: Civic groups call for sweeping reforms to restore falling trust, which experts have linked to a resurgence of populist "protest" voting at the expense of the major parties.

items.title: MPs push gambling ad ban as study reveals targeting of women
items.description: Gambling is being promoted as fun, social and "harmless" for women through social media and lifestyle marketing, in a shift researchers warn is normalising betting and obscuring the risks.

items.title: 'Here if you need': Ashton Hurn played a short and difficult game in the SA election
items.description: Sport and politics are similar. Good players work hard and perform well under pressure, something SA Liberal Leader Ashton Hurn has been credited for. But the party's disastrous election results show just how difficult the game can be.

items.title: Bill Cosby ordered to pay $US19m for historical sexual assault
items.description: A civil jury in California awards a woman $US19.25 million after finding Bill Cosby liable for sexually assaulting her.
